sn46.54:4.2: ‘Come, reverends, give up these five hindrances, corruptions of the heart that weaken wisdom, and meditate spreading a heart full of love to one direction …
sn46.54:4.5: meditate spreading a heart full of equanimity to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth.
sn46.54:4.6: In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, spread a heart full of equanimity to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.’
sn46.54:6.1: “Sir, this morning we robed up and, taking our bowls and robes, entered Haliddavasana for alms.
sn46.54:6.2: Then, sir, it occurred to us,
sn46.54:6.3: ‘It’s too early to wander for alms in Haliddavasana.
sn46.54:7.1: Why don’t we visit the monastery for the wanderers of other religions?’ So, sir, we went to the monastery for the wanderers of other religions and exchanged greetings with the wanderers there.
sn46.54:7.2: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, we sat down to one side. Then, sir, the wanderers said to us:
sn46.54:8.1: ‘Reverends, the ascetic Gotama teaches his disciples like this:
sn46.54:8.2: “Come, mendicants, give up these five hindrances, corruptions of the heart that weaken wisdom, and meditate spreading a heart full of love to one direction …
sn46.54:8.5: meditate spreading a heart full of equanimity to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, spread a heart full of equanimity to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.’
sn46.54:9.1: We too teach our disciples in just the same way.
sn46.54:9.2: ‘Come, reverends, give up these five hindrances, corruptions of the heart that weaken wisdom, and meditate spreading a heart full of love to one direction …
sn46.54:9.5: meditate spreading a heart full of equanimity to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, spread a heart full of equanimity to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.’
sn46.54:9.6: What, then, is the difference between the ascetic Gotama’s teaching and instruction and ours?
sn46.54:10.1: Then, sir, we neither approved nor rejected that statement of the wanderers of other religions. Without approving or rejecting it, we rose from our seats, thinking:
sn46.54:10.2: ‘We will learn the meaning of this statement from the Buddha himself.’”
